question:
Assertion (A): If $F(x)$ is an antiderivative of $f(x)$, then $\int_{a}^{b} f(x) dx$ depends only on $F(a)$ and $F(b)$, not on the choice of antiderivative.

Reason (R): All antiderivatives of $f(x)$ differ by a constant, so when calculating $F(b)-F(a)$ the constant cancels.
explanation:
If $F(x)$ is an antiderivative of $f(x)$ then $\int_a^b f(x)dx = F(b)-F(a)$.

Any other antiderivative is $F(x)+C$. Then $(F(b)+C)-(F(a)+C)=F(b)-F(a)$.

Thus the constant cancels and the value of the definite integral is unchanged.

Therefore both the assertion and reason are true and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and the Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
